title: Gordon vs SPU: tuition, size, location
summary: Gordon College (Gordon) versus Seattle Pacific University (SPU). Also searched as SPU vs Gordon. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Seattle Pacific University and Gordon College are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership codes reported by College Scorecard. Seattle Pacific University, located in Seattle, has a larger undergraduate enrollment of 1,762 students compared to Gordon College's 1,278 students in Wenham. Tuition costs also differ, with Seattle Pacific University charging $40,407 for in-state tuition, while Gordon College's in-state tuition is $30,700. These distinctions highlight differences in size, location, and cost between the two universities.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Seattle Pacific University versus Gordon College shows a notable difference in tuition costs. Seattle Pacific University charges $40,407 for both in-state and out-of-state tuition, whereas Gordon College's tuition is $30,700 for both in-state and out-of-state students. Regarding student debt, the median debt for completers at Seattle Pacific University is $24,000, which is slightly lower than Gordon College's median debt of $26,250. These figures provide insight into the financial commitments associated with attending each institution.

paragraphs: Seattle Pacific University versus Gordon College (SPU vs Gordon) differ in their learning environments and campus settings. These differences in location and campus size may influence the student experience and learning model at each institution.
